verdict.reasoning: Patient reports feeling short of breath starting over the last hour while sitting and watching TV: "over the last hour, I've started to feel, like, a bit short of breath" and "This is while you're sitting watching tv?" "Yeah."

The note states the patient is 43 years old, but the transcript shows a DOB of 20/04/1980 and correction to 1983; age is never explicitly calculated. The rest (female, one-hour SOB at rest watching TV) is supported, but the specific age "43-year-old" is not and could be incorrect based on the DOB.

The patient reports a cough starting yesterday and denies bringing anything up: "So I started with a cough yesterday" and "Have you brought anything up?" "No, I haven't. No." This supports a new non-productive (dry) cough.
The patient is four weeks post-cesarean: "I had a C section a few weeks ago." and when asked how long: "Yeah. Four weeks."
She took codeine regularly after the C-section and stopped about a week ago: "They gave me some codeine." and "Yeah, I've been taking that fairly regularly, but probably haven't taken it for a week."
She endorses chest soreness with deep inspiration: when asked, "How about when you take a very deep breath in?" she replies, "I mean, yeah, my chest feels sore..."
She notes tenderness at the C-section scar: "my chest feels sore, but so does my C section scar. You know, it's all tender."

She reports feeling her heart racing and feeling stressed: "I feel like I'm getting really stressed out because, like, my heart is really going." and the doctor clarifies "you're feeling your heart more than normal?" "Yeah." This supports palpitations and stress related to increased heart rate.
She denies previous similar episodes of SOB: when asked if she noticed anything like this before, she answers "No."
She denies chest pain at rest: "And the shortness of breath, does it cause any pain in your chest?" "No."
When asked about other medical problems, she denies any: "And apart from the C section and the shortness of breath. Have you got any other medical problems I should know about?" "No."
The medication history matches: "They gave me some codeine." and "I've been taking that fairly regularly, but probably haven't taken it for a week."
Allergy and unknown reaction are documented: "And are you allergic?" "I'm allergic to ibuprofen, though." When asked what happens, she states, "I don't know."

From the counted pulse: 30 beats over the timed interval, and the doctor states, "your heart is running slightly fast." This indicates mild tachycardia; 180 bpm is not mentioned and would not be described as "slightly fast."
No temperature or fever is mentioned anywhere in the transcript; stating that no fever was documented is consistent with the absence of such information.

The patient has acute SOB and cough, 4 weeks post C-section, and the doctor expresses concern for clots in the lungs: "Given that you've had a C section and you're short of breath... it might be worth you going into the hospital" and later, "some people can suffer with clots... in your lungs." This aligns with concern to rule out pulmonary embolism.

The doctor attributes the slightly fast heart rate to SOB and pain/distress: "your heart is running slightly fast at the moment, which is probably because of your shortness of breath and some of the pain that you're under."
She is 4 weeks post C-section with scar tenderness: "Yeah. Four weeks." and "my C section scar... it's all tender." This supports a postoperative state four weeks after cesarean with scar tenderness.

The doctor advises urgent hospital evaluation but does not specify a "pulmonary embolism workup including imaging and laboratory tests": "it might be worth you going into the hospital to get checked out a bit further." The specific mention of PE workup, imaging, and labs is not stated.
The doctor recommends withholding codeine: "And if you're taking any medications, like codeine, don't take them for the time being."

She is instructed to self-present promptly with her baby: the doctor offers ambulance vs self-transport, and she chooses self: "I'll go. I'll take myself." The doctor agrees and adds, "go fairly quickly and take some bits for baby at the same time."

The doctor explains risk of clots after C-section and need for assessment and treatment: "given that you've had a C section, some people can suffer with clots... in your lungs" and "it's not something to worry about, but needs to be checked out in the hospital first" and "they can give you something to reduce the clot." This constitutes education about PE risk and need for prompt diagnosis/treatment.
